title: Fast-path SDKs: presets and lossy-network rundown
content:
Purpose
This is a working notes doc for a compact "fast-path" SDK onramp: opinionated presets and a small set of CLI lab exercises focused on realistic failure modes (lossy networks, transient auth failures, and mixed latency). The goal is to produce a 10–15 minute dev loop that demonstrates production-facing behaviors without overwhelming new users.

Scope and constraints
- Target audience: backend engineers and full-stack product engineers who want to ship a Redwood-backed LLM feature quickly.
- Platform coverage: Node, Python, and a lightweight CLI shim that mirrors direct HTTP usage.
- Non-goals: full API surface coverage, advanced routing policies, Dedicated deployment onboarding.

What success looks like (early measurable signals)
- New devs can get a token, run 3 simple examples (chat, generation, embeddings) in < 15 minutes.
- CLI labs include a reproducible network-loss test that reproduces a token-level retry and fallback event.
- Telemetry shows SDK instrumented spans and a simple error taxonomy in Console (auth_error, network_timeout, model_degraded).

Opinionated presets (starter configs)
- dev-fast: single-call, streaming enabled, low-batch (batch=1), relaxed safety checks for dev environments.
  - Purpose: fastest iteration.
  - Warning in README: not for prod.
- staging-sane: batching enabled (batch=8), KV cache enabled, latency SLO 200ms p50, 600ms p95.
  - Purpose: mimic typical customer staging usage.
- prod-conservative: batching=auto, cache=enabled, fallback_models=[small-quantized], retry_policy={max_retries:2, backoff_ms:200}.
  - Purpose: safe defaults for early production adoption.

CLI labs (short exercises for a 30–45 minute hands-on session)
- Lab 1: Quickstart (5–7 min)
  - Steps: install rdw-cli, rdw auth login (paste token), run rdw generate "summarize this README" --preset dev-fast.
  - Observation goals: streaming works, token billing printed, simple latency stat.
- Lab 2: Embeddings + similarity (8–10 min)
  - Steps: create local dataset (3 docs), run rdw embed --preset dev-fast, run example similarity search.
  - Observation: cost per unit displayed, delta when switching to staging-sane.
- Lab 3: Lossy network simulation (12–15 min) — the unique bit
  - Intent: exercise retries, fallbacks, idempotency and partial responses.
  - Setup: rdw-cli has a --network-sim flag that toggles a local proxy script (node/python proxy included in examples/) which simulates 0.5–5s added latency, random packet drops (5–30% per request), and truncated streaming frames.
  - Steps: run proxy with --drop-rate=0.2 --latency-ms=800, run a streaming generation, watch SDK client-side retry and automatic fallback to model variant.
  - Checkpoints: SDK logs should contain a retry span, Console shows a fallback event, and client receives a graceful partial response rather than an abrupt error.
  - Notes: this lab intentionally surfaces the boundaries of current SDK behavior (we expect a few TODOs in the implementation).

SDK behavior expectations and helpful messages
- On transient network issues: expose a structured error type with fields (code string, retryable boolean, attempt_count). The CLI should render a short human message plus a copyable JSON blob for debug.
- On fallback: log "fallback invoked: reason=<reason>, from=<model>, to=<fallback>" and emit a telemetry event with the prompt id.
- On truncated streaming: surface a "partial_output" marker and include advice to re-run with --resume-cursor if available.

Telemetry & observability checklist for the labs
- Minimal spans: request.prepare, request.send, request.receive, retry.attempt, fallback.trigger.
- Attach tags: preset.name, model.name, region, network.sim=true/false.
- Demo dashboard widgets: 1) lab traffic p95/p99 latency 2) retry rate over time 3) fallback count and top reasons.

Developer notes / implementation TODOs
- CLI: implement --network-sim proxy wrapper (reference proxy in examples/network-proxy/) — currently a PoC in PR 128.
- SDK: add structured errors and expose .retryable on exceptions (Python and Node parity needed).
- Docs: quickstart README must include a short section on what to expect under simulated packet loss (copy of this doc).
- Testing: add e2e test that runs the proxy in CI with a stable seed and asserts the client recovers within 2 retries. (flaky risk — limit to nightly).

Open questions and trade-offs (bulleted, to resolve in next sync)
- How opinionated should presets be vs. exposing everything as knobs? We want safe-but-simple defaults for fast-path.
- Should the --network-sim tool be part of the main package or a separate examples/ utility? Separate seems simpler for releases.
- For streaming truncation semantics: does the server emit an end-of-stream marker for truncated frames or do we rely on client heuristics? Who owns reassembly?

User-facing copy snippets (for README and first-run UI)
- Short: "Start in 3 commands: install, rdw auth login, rdw generate --preset dev-fast"
- Longer (README intro): "The fast-path presets give a friction-free way to explore the Redwood API. Use dev-fast for quick iteration, staging-sane to test batching and cache effects, and prod-conservative as a safe template for production rollouts. The CLI labs include a lossy-network simulator so you can see how the SDK behaves under real-world conditions (timeouts, partial streams, and fallbacks)."

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: network-sim introduces flaky behaviors that leak into CI. Mitigation: mark CI e2e as optional/nightly and pin deterministic seeds.
- Risk: dev-fast encourages skipping safety checks. Mitigation: include bright red warnings in CLI output and README; require explicit --force to bypass safety for certain endpoints.

Next steps (owner + ETA)
- Implement structured errors in Node SDK — owner: Liam O'Connor — ETA: 2025-02-10
- Deliver CLI network proxy PoC into examples/ — owner: Diego Alvarez — ETA: 2025-02-05 (PR 128 in review)
- Draft README and lab exercise script — owner: Maya Chen — ETA: 2025-02-03 (this doc captures first draft)

Appendix: quick proxy usage (developer copy-paste)
- Start proxy (python): python examples/network-proxy/proxy.py --drop-rate 0.2 --latency-ms 800 --seed 42
- Run a streaming example: rdw generate --preset dev-fast --stream --prompt "Write a 150-word product blurb"

Notes to self
- Keep labs under 45 minutes total for workshops.
- Solicit feedback from Solutions Eng next week for example prompts and failure playbook.

-- end of draft --
